translations.01673def9c55673dbfa34828f385b384f879b062: [NDRC Chairman Zheng Shanjie: Firmly Implement the Strategy of Expanding Domestic Demand] NDRC Chairman Zheng Shanjie wrote in an article published in Study Times that the strategy of expanding domestic demand should be firmly implemented. The expansion of domestic demand should be better coordinated with deepening supply-side structural reform to strengthen the momentum and reliability of the domestic economic cycle. The fundamental role of consumption in economic growth should be fully leveraged. Urban and rural residents' incomes should be increased through multiple channels, consumption of major items such as automobiles should be stabilised, new-energy vehicles should be promoted in rural areas, and new growth areas in consumption, including green consumption and service consumption, should be fostered and expanded. The key role of investment in optimising the supply structure should be further strengthened. Implementation of the 102 major projects under the 14th Five-Year Plan and other major economic and social projects should be accelerated; major infrastructure and new infrastructure construction in areas including energy, water conservancy and transport should be advanced; the guiding role of government investment and policy incentives should be leveraged; and the vitality of private investment should be effectively stimulated.

translations.078bd99dee2d022bdaa37fc6592b37bdfd24600a: The General Office of the State Council recently issued Guiding Opinions, planning to basically establish a high-quality charging infrastructure system by 2030 in order to address the problem of "charging anxiety" in the development of new-energy vehicles. At the same time, various forms of private capital are encouraged to participate in investment, operational service standards are to be improved, and technological research and commercial cooperation are to be promoted. translations.097588690568cc35ea27d5eb94f3715f31e8466f: On June 21, Vice Minister of Finance Xu Hongcai announced at a State Council regular policy briefing that the vehicle purchase-tax reduction and exemption policy for new-energy vehicles would be extended through the end of 2027. From January 1, 2024 to December 31, 2025, new-energy vehicles will be exempt from vehicle purchase tax, with a maximum tax exemption of RMB 30,000 per vehicle; from 2026 through 2027, vehicle purchase tax will be levied at half the normal rate, with a maximum tax reduction of RMB 15,000 per vehicle. The policy is expected to reduce vehicle purchase tax by approximately RMB 520 billion in total from 2024 to 2027. The policy is intended to further promote the adoption of new-energy vehicles and adapt to market demand, with lower-priced models receiving a greater degree of tax relief. According to the latest data, the market penetration rate of new-energy vehicles continues to rise, with production and sales increasing significantly.

translations.0afc612b8d376b2b99f86dc21d1a243f4ccabcb8: On June 15, the People's Bank of China announced that it would lower the medium-term lending facility (MLF) rate by 10 basis points to 2.65% and conduct RMB 237 billion of one-year MLF operations, resulting in a net injection of RMB 37 billion. Analysts noted that, following the reduction in policy rates, lending rates for enterprises and households may fall further, particularly against the backdrop of a weakening property market. translations.1affc3313179a89e3871adffd653b0f6be12b741: On June 21, the Ministry of Finance, the State Taxation Administration and the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology jointly issued an announcement extending the vehicle purchase-tax reduction and exemption policy for new-energy vehicles: new-energy vehicles purchased from January 1, 2024 to December 31, 2025 will be exempt from vehicle purchase tax, while those purchased from 2026 through 2027 will be taxed at half the normal rate. This is the fourth extension of the previous vehicle purchase-tax preferential policy, which has been implemented progressively since 2014 to stimulate the market. According to preliminary estimates, the extension will bring the total scale of vehicle purchase-tax reductions and exemptions from 2024 to 2027 to RMB 520 billion. In addition, the announcement sets a maximum tax exemption of RMB 30,000 per new-energy passenger vehicle and a maximum tax reduction of RMB 15,000 for the half-rate period, in order to guide the market more precisely. The policy also includes relevant provisions for battery-swapping models. The news drove up Hong Kong-listed new-energy vehicle stocks.

translations.1ca66b60f1a84e1655e2c2298f485fb044d45fd7: [Xi Jinping Chairs the Second Meeting of the Central Commission for Comprehensively Deepening Reform, Emphasising the Establishment of a Higher-Standard Open-Economy System and Promoting a Gradual Shift from Dual Controls on Energy Consumption to Dual Controls on Carbon Emissions] Xi Jinping, General Secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, President of China, Chairman of the Central Military Commission, and Director of the Central Commission for Comprehensively Deepening Reform, chaired the second meeting of the Central Commission for Comprehensively Deepening Reform on the afternoon of July 11. The meeting reviewed and approved the Opinions on Establishing a Higher-Standard Open-Economy System to Promote the Creation of a New Development Pattern, the Implementation Plan for Deepening Rural Reform, the Opinions on Promoting a Gradual Shift from Dual Controls on Energy Consumption to Dual Controls on Carbon Emissions, the Opinions on Piloting Reform of the Remuneration System at Higher-Education Institutions and Research Institutes, the Implementation Opinions on Further Deepening Reform of the Oil and Gas Market System and Enhancing the Country's Capacity to Safeguard Oil and Gas Security, and the Guiding Opinions on Deepening Power-System Reform and Accelerating the Establishment of a New Power System. translations.1dc9a99e227ee770536d410a7627ec7a32bba649: The Monetary Policy Committee of the People's Bank of China recently held its regular meeting for the second quarter of 2023 and put forward important views including intensifying countercyclical adjustments, the loan-support programme for ensuring the delivery of pre-sold homes, and an action plan to support financing for technology companies. translations.33289805e533e7abccf72d3eb56142f6198e414e: The Monetary Policy Committee of the People's Bank of China held its regular meeting for the second quarter of 2023 in Beijing on June 28. The new wording, 'endogenous momentum remains weak and demand-driven growth remains insufficient,' reflected sluggish growth in consumption and investment. The central bank stressed that it would intensify macro-policy regulation, implement prudent monetary policy, and support the expansion of domestic demand and improvement of the consumption environment. At the same time, to address the risk of renminbi depreciation, the meeting proposed stabilising the exchange rate and deepening market-oriented reforms. In addition, price trends received attention, although the CPI was expected to rise gradually in the second half of the year.
translations.333f1cca0bb8c098531136d6caa6e30620b553bd: The People's Bank of China recently lowered the medium-term lending facility (MLF) operation rate and the seven-day reverse-repurchase rate, and market participants generally believe this may mark the beginning of an interest-rate-cut cycle. Analysts noted that the rate cuts were intended to stimulate the economy and alleviate weak credit demand. Although the rate cuts were a positive signal, experts believed that more policy support was still needed to boost economic vitality, including reducing the reserve requirement ratio and strengthening support measures for sectors such as property. At the same time, the market expected the LPR to be adjusted accordingly in the future to promote further credit growth.
translations.338a16bbccddc9b54f799429908658681756d2b2: On June 15, the People's Bank of China announced a 10-basis-point reduction in the medium-term lending facility (MLF) rate, after the seven-day reverse-repurchase rate had also fallen. translations.35ed4d767f53f776e5c4c14a9db5dc1cd040bf09: [Central Bank: Further Unblock the Monetary-Policy Transmission Mechanism and Maintain Reasonably Ample Liquidity] The Monetary Policy Committee of the central bank held its regular meeting for the second quarter of 2023. It called for continuing to make good use of funds already deployed through policy-based and development-oriented financial instruments, enhancing the guiding role of government investment and policy incentives, and effectively driving and stimulating private investment. It called for monitoring marginal changes in price trends and keeping the overall price level broadly stable. It called for maintaining the stability of relending and rediscount instruments, extending the implementation of the support instrument for inclusive loans to micro and small businesses and the loan-support programme for ensuring delivery of pre-sold homes, continuing to increase support for key fields and weak links in the national economy such as inclusive finance, green development, technological innovation, and infrastructure construction, and using a combination of measures to support coordinated regional development.

translations.3655ee58256d4e8a6aa0429a57451cbd58f341a1: [New-Energy Vehicle Purchase-Tax Relief Policy Introduced; Li Auto: No Excuse for Failing to Meet the Target; NIO: Huge Advantage over Luxury Fuel Vehicles] On June 21, the Ministry of Finance, the State Taxation Administration, and the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology jointly issued the Announcement on Extending and Optimising the Vehicle Purchase-Tax Relief Policy for New-Energy Vehicles. It specified that purchases of new-energy vehicles in 2024-2025 would be exempt from vehicle purchase tax, while purchases in 2026-2027 would be subject to half the tax. In response, NIO and Li Auto, representatives of China's new generation of new-energy vehicle manufacturers, quickly responded positively and welcomed the new policy. 'This is excellent. It directly provides four years of policy stability, so our team has no excuse for failing to achieve the company's 2025 strategic goals. Sell 1.6 million vehicles and generate revenue of RMB 500 billion in 2025, to be verified at the beginning of 2026!' said Li Xiang, founder and chairman of Li Auto. A relevant NIO representative said that from now until 2027, battery-electric vehicles would continue to enjoy vehicle purchase-tax relief, giving NIO a huge advantage over luxury fuel vehicles in terms of purchase cost. After the new purchase-tax policy for battery-electric vehicles takes effect, under the new policy NIO's separation of vehicle and battery through its battery-swapping model can clearly help users lower the cost of buying a vehicle and reduce vehicle purchase-tax expenditure at the time of purchase. translations.3cde5c77854919f4b4b8224c3f3d3c42fbda593f: [Columbia Professor: Commercial Property Caught in a 'Doom Loop' That Will Trigger a New Banking Crisis] Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh, a professor of real estate and finance at Columbia Business School, warned of an 'urban doom loop' in commercial property. translations.43689586fe61326affdeac81767793102d7c83be: [NDRC Chairman: Give Industrial Security Greater Prominence and Strengthen Breakthroughs in Key Core Technologies and Support from Strategic Resources] Zheng Shanjie, Chairman of the National Development and Reform Commission, published a signed article in Qiushi entitled 'Accelerating the Construction of a Modern Industrial System Supported by the Real Economy.' An industrial system without security safeguards will inevitably be exposed to all kinds of risks and challenges, so security and development must be advanced in parallel. translations.6166573948b2df2122ee76c1105e7196c4ae6404: On June 20, 2023, the People's Bank of China announced the loan prime rates (LPRs): the one-year LPR was 3.55% and the LPR for terms of more than five years was 4.2%, both down 10 basis points. These were the first reductions since August 2022. The rate cuts were mainly influenced by reductions in bank deposit rates, with demand- and time-deposit rates lowered by 5 to 15 basis points. The adjustments were expected to reduce households' housing-loan costs and boost property demand. They would also help improve financing demand in the real economy and stimulate growth in credit and investment. Although asymmetric rate cuts had been expected, the two LPR maturities were ultimately reduced by the same amount, demonstrating a prudent and measured policy approach. Looking ahead, subsequent fiscal and industrial policies were expected to follow in order to promote economic recovery.

translations.6447c814fbc1684ff1998a6061675e1990b3d12f: On June 21, the State Council Information Office held a press conference to introduce policies promoting high-quality development of the new-energy vehicle industry. Xin Guobin, Vice Minister of Industry and Information Technology, disclosed that in the first five months of this year, production and sales of new-energy vehicles reached 3.005 million and 2.94 million, respectively, representing year-on-year growth of 45.1% and 46.8%. To support development of the industry, the Ministry of Finance extended the vehicle purchase-tax relief policy for new-energy vehicles through the end of 2027 and set a maximum tax exemption of RMB 30,000 for each new-energy passenger vehicle, with half the tax to be levied from 2026. The policy was expected to provide total vehicle purchase-tax relief of RMB 520 billion from 2024 to 2027. These measures were intended to stabilise market expectations, encourage consumption, and promote high-quality development of the industry.

translations.65c38d42adb15eb191371430bbb86e60b1d5debc: [NDRC Chairman Zheng Shanjie: Resolutely Prevent Systemic Risks, with a Focus on Four Major Areas of Security] Zheng Shanjie, Secretary of the Leading Party Members Group and Chairman of the National Development and Reform Commission, wrote that systemic risks must be resolutely prevented, positive interaction between high-quality development and high-level security must be promoted, and the new development pattern must be safeguarded through a new security framework. The focus must be on four major areas of security. First is food security. The system under which both Party committees and governments assume responsibility for food security and for protecting cultivated land must be strictly implemented; a new round of action to increase grain-production capacity by 100 billion jin must be carried out; coordinated safeguards for grain production, purchasing, storage, processing, and sales must be continuously strengthened; mechanisms to safeguard the income of grain farmers and compensate principal producing regions must be improved; every effort must be made to ensure grain supply and stable prices; and the foundations of food security must be comprehensively consolidated. Second is energy and resource security. The energy revolution must be advanced in depth, planning and construction of a new energy system accelerated, and systems for energy production, supply, storage, and sales strengthened. Resource exploration and development must be intensified. Construction of the national reserve system must be strengthened, and the reserve layout and facility network optimised and improved. Third is the security and stability of industrial and supply chains. The role of key enterprises and key industrial parks in maintaining the security and stability of industrial and supply chains must be brought into play, and projects to connect industrial and supply chains must be implemented. The core competitiveness of manufacturing must be enhanced, actions to strengthen and supplement chains implemented in depth, weak links in industrial chains reinforced, a number of areas of industrial-chain strength forged, and optimisation and upgrading of entire industrial chains promoted. Fourth is data security. Construction of the data-security safeguard system must be strengthened, security must run through the entire data-governance process, and national data security must be effectively protected.

translations.6c839fcffb7591e341073d2430c9bdfc49c9c410: Landun Zhuantui formally entered the delisting-consolidation period, becoming the first convertible bond in history to be mandatorily delisted. translations.7027a88417b8eaca3377e4e7c0a032b82a79d40a: [NDRC Chairman Zheng Shanjie: Adhere to the Direction of Socialist Market-Economy Reform] In an article published in Study Times, Zheng Shanjie, Chairman of the National Development and Reform Commission, stated that the direction of socialist market-economy reform must be upheld and that effective markets and a well-functioning government must be better combined. The 'two unwavering commitments' must be upheld. Reform of state-owned capital and state-owned enterprises must be deepened; state capital and state-owned enterprises must become stronger, better, and larger; the environment for the development of private enterprises must be optimised; implementation of policy measures to promote the development and growth of the private economy must be accelerated; the rights and interests of foreign investors must be protected according to law; and legal and regulatory obstacles and hidden barriers affecting fair competition and common development among enterprises under all forms of ownership must be removed. The foundational institutions of the market economy must be improved. Institution-building and supervision in areas such as protection of property rights, market access, fair competition, and social credit must be strengthened, as must antitrust and action against unfair competition. Construction of a unified national market must be accelerated. Market-oriented reform of factors of production must be deepened, construction of a modern infrastructure system and a high-standard market system advanced in a coordinated manner, and a first-class market-oriented, law-based, and internationalised business environment created.

translations.900f7265fd8867d030a3b943228a0696453a37d3:
[Li Qiang: Promptly Implement a Group of Highly Targeted, Combined, and Coordinated Policy Measures Focused on Stabilising Growth, Stabilising Employment, and Preventing Risks] Li Qiang, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Premier of the State Council, chaired a symposium with experts on the economic situation on the afternoon of July 6 to hear experts' and scholars' views and recommendations on the current economic situation and economic work.

Ding Xuexiang, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Vice Premier of the State Council, attended.

At the symposium, experts and scholars including Liu Shangxi, Luo Zhiheng, Tian Xuan, Huang Xianhai, Yuan Haixia, Qin Hailin, Lu Ming, and Zhao Wei spoke in turn. They believed that, in a complex and severe external environment, China's economic development had demonstrated tremendous resilience and that there should be full confidence in the prospects for China's economic development. They also offered views and recommendations on resolving problems in economic operations.

After listening carefully to the experts and scholars, Li Qiang stated that, since the beginning of this year, under the strong leadership of the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core, China's economy had shown a trend of recovery and improvement. At the same time, it was necessary to recognise that the global political and economic situation was complex and had many effects on China's development. The current economic situation must be assessed comprehensively, dialectically, and from a long-term perspective, while maintaining strategic resolve and strengthening confidence in development.

Li Qiang stated that China was at a critical stage of economic recovery and industrial upgrading. The general principle of pursuing progress while ensuring stability must be upheld, the new development philosophy implemented fully, accurately, and comprehensively, and creation of the new development pattern accelerated. A group of highly targeted, combined, and coordinated policy measures focused on stabilising growth, stabilising employment, and preventing risks must be implemented promptly. Greater efforts must be made to transform the development model, adjust the economic structure, and increase growth momentum, centred on the primary task of high-quality development. Regular communication and exchange mechanisms between the government and all kinds of enterprises, including private and foreign-invested enterprises, must be established and improved, and more scientific decision-making achieved by increasing interaction in work.

Li Qiang expressed the hope that experts and scholars would apply their professional strengths, understand objective laws and overall development trends, offer more constructive views and recommendations, and contribute their wisdom and strength to promoting high-quality development. (CCTV)

translations.a263f197bb8244d1be5e061eaee079238d40b50d: On June 20, the central bank lowered the loan prime rates (LPRs), reducing the one-year LPR to 3.55% and the LPR for terms of more than five years to 4.2%, each down 10 basis points. Analysis indicated that the adjustment would lower housing-loan rates, ease the burden on homebuyers, and might raise confidence in housing consumption. translations.a311f753e99b63df2ce3d23aca55d498af883b32: [China Securities Journal Front Page: LPRs Cut by 10 Basis Points as Monetary Policy Continues to Exert Force; More Policy Tools Expected, with Room Remaining for Cuts to the Reserve Requirement Ratio and Interest Rates] The National Interbank Funding Center, authorised by the People's Bank of China, announced on June 20 that the one-year loan prime rate (LPR) was 3.55% and the LPR for terms of more than five years was 4.2%, both down 10 basis points from the previous period. Experts believed that lower LPRs would drive bank lending rates lower, thereby stimulating financing demand in the real economy and bolstering confidence in the property market. To help stabilise growth, monetary policy was expected to be intensified further, with cuts to the reserve requirement ratio and interest rates still possible during the year.

It called for advancing construction of the Guangzhou Futures Exchange, the Greater Bay Area bond platform, Nansha International Financial Island, and Shenzhen-Hong Kong International Financial City; conducting agricultural-product trading through existing trading venues; and creating important financial platforms serving high-quality economic development and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. translations.af4ff2590c13ddca3c04c6c188e6951ddf2afa0b: On June 15, the People's Bank of China announced that, to maintain liquidity in the banking system, it would conduct a RMB 237 billion medium-term lending facility (MLF) operation and a RMB 2 billion reverse-repurchase operation, with the MLF rate lowered by 10 basis points to 2.65%. translations.b0a4df15935fc910a72fc91218738a55f1e164ce: [CSRC Launches Reform of Public-Fund Fee Rates, Covering Six Areas] It was learned from the regulatory authorities that the China Securities Regulatory Commission had launched reform of public-fund fee rates, mainly covering six areas. First, products with fixed fee rates would remain the principal type. Second, more products with floating fee rates would be introduced. The CSRC had previously accepted a group of floating-fee-rate products linked to investors' holding periods. Recently, it formally received fundraising applications for 11 floating-fee-rate products in two categories: those linked to fund size and those linked to fund performance. Third, fee-rate levels for actively managed equity funds would be reduced. Fourth, securities-trading commission rates for public funds would be reduced. The related reform measures involved amendments to relevant regulations and were expected to be completed before the end of 2023. Fifth, charges in the sale of public funds would be standardised. This was expected to be completed before the end of 2024. Sixth, the fee-rate disclosure mechanism for the public-fund industry would be improved. (Securities Times)

translations.c213a7ca558532c10a02a74992e5348cce044edc: [LPR for Terms of More Than Five Years Falls by 10 Basis Points; Payments on a RMB 1 Million, 30-Year Mortgage Fall by RMB 21,000] The latest loan prime rates (LPRs) were announced today, with the five-year LPR lowered to 4.2% from 4.3%. translations.c3e19664990258dfe8633cabb3995a19ffe0f9e0: [Li Qiang: The Trend of China's Economic Recovery and Improvement Is Clear, and the Expected Growth Target of About 5% Is Likely to Be Achieved for the Full Year] Premier Li Qiang attended the opening ceremony of the 2023 Summer Davos Forum in Tianjin on the morning of the 27th and delivered a speech. Li said that, over a longer period in the future, China would continue to provide powerful momentum for global economic recovery and growth. China remains the world's largest developing country. We have a population of more than 1.4 billion, while per-capita economic indicators and people's living standards are not yet high, and development remains unbalanced and inadequate; however, therein also lie China's development potential and room for growth. We are earnestly implementing the new development philosophy, accelerating creation of a new development pattern, and working to achieve high-quality development. We will introduce more practical and effective measures in areas including expanding the potential of domestic demand, stimulating market vitality, promoting coordinated urban-rural and regional development, accelerating the green transformation of the development model, and promoting high-standard opening up. These measures are taking effect. Judging from developments so far this year, the trend of China's economic recovery and improvement is clear. The economy grew by 4.5% year on year in the first quarter, growth in the second quarter is expected to be faster than in the first quarter, and the expected growth target of about 5% is likely to be achieved for the full year. Some international organisations and institutions have also raised their forecasts for China's economic growth this year, demonstrating confidence in China's development prospects. We have every confidence and ability to promote the steady and sustained progress of China's economy along the path of high-quality development over a relatively long cycle. This will continuously expand the size of the market, create opportunities for cooperation, and provide an unending source of momentum for global economic recovery and growth, while also providing investors from all countries with opportunities for mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation.

translations.d0ecd6ccf3bd88ffc22f29d6d49943b812eb0b60: After remaining unchanged for nine consecutive periods, China's loan prime rates (LPRs) were lowered for the first time on June 20. The one-year LPR was 3.55% and the LPR for terms of more than five years was 4.2%, both down 10 basis points. The adjustment benefited from the central bank's frequent recent interest-rate cuts, which created conditions for lower LPRs. Analysts believed the LPR reductions would help strengthen countercyclical adjustment, promote a recovery in demand, and might stimulate credit demand and enhance market confidence. translations.d2270cad87ce68cbc6d6a2b5a8840df2e5a328f0: In the early hours of Thursday, the Federal Reserve announced that it would maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5.00%-5.25%, the first pause in rate increases since March last year. The Federal Reserve said the decision would allow the committee to assess more data and stressed that it would remain committed to returning inflation to the 2% target. According to the latest dot plot, the median interest-rate projection for the end of 2023 was raised to 5.6%, suggesting that two further rate increases remained possible. At the same time, the Federal Reserve lowered its GDP growth forecasts for 2024 and 2025 and made corresponding adjustments to its forecasts for unemployment and personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation, with PCE inflation expected to be 3.2% in 2023.
translations.d2d1639dbe2063df536fc7c0103d7841b5300ea1: The Ministry of Finance, the State Taxation Administration, and the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology recently issued an announcement extending the vehicle purchase-tax relief policy for new-energy vehicles through the end of 2027. From 2024 to 2025, new-energy passenger vehicles will be exempt from vehicle purchase tax, with a maximum exemption of RMB 30,000 per vehicle; from 2026 to 2027, half the tax will be levied, with a maximum tax reduction of RMB 15,000 per vehicle. Following implementation, the policy is expected to provide cumulative relief of RMB 520 billion from 2024 to 2027. Since 2014, the policy has been extended several times and has effectively promoted the market development of new-energy vehicles. In the first five months of this year, both production and sales of new-energy vehicles achieved significant growth. Relevant experts believed the policy would continue to stimulate automobile consumption and promote the transition from fuel vehicles to new-energy vehicles.

translations.d35e03f1dc4625977f08407799ff172ab318294a: After earlier declines, sentiment in the A-share market improved markedly last week. translations.d422dba5525bada71faf99754b0bee448465ddcc: [LPRs May Be Cut Asymmetrically] With the MLF rate cut implemented, several people also expected that a corresponding reduction in the LPRs in June would be highly probable. Interest rates on existing and incremental loans benchmarked to the LPRs will fall to varying degrees, driving further declines in financing costs in the real economy and accelerating the stimulation of domestic demand.' translations.d74c3763600bf2a40221bbd94e45e453bc8cc686: Since June, China has entered a new interest-rate-cut cycle covering deposits, open-market operations and the MLF, LPRs, and other areas. translations.da3867e25935f1326c70d7f50f311a6eb3bd448a: [NDRC Chairman Zheng Shanjie: Remove Institutional Obstacles Restricting Private Enterprises' Fair Participation in Market Competition and Further Expand Market Access for Private Investment] Zheng Shanjie, Secretary of the Leading Party Members Group and Chairman of the National Development and Reform Commission, wrote that a combination of measures must be used to expand demand. Implementation of the strategy to expand domestic demand must be organically combined with deepening supply-side structural reform. The sustained recovery of consumption must be promoted, traditional consumption continuously upgraded, new forms of consumption cultivated more rapidly, and consumption hotspots continuously expanded. Effective investment must be actively expanded, the structure of investment from the central budget optimised, and resources concentrated on major, difficult, and urgent matters. Construction of the 102 major projects in the 14th Five-Year Plan must be advanced forcefully and in an orderly manner; institutional obstacles restricting private enterprises' fair participation in market competition must be removed; the scope of market access for private investment further expanded; and more private capital encouraged and attracted to participate in national major projects and projects addressing weak links.
translations.da5dbd8e5156013a851a57d3f502712768c0ed06: [LPR 'Rate Cuts' Implemented as Banks in Many Locations Follow with Mortgage-Rate Reductions] After nine months without action, China's loan prime rates (LPRs) were reduced again, and mortgage rates around the country were adjusted accordingly. Analyst Wang Qing noted that the reductions were intended to address insufficient momentum in the economic recovery and a weakening property market, and expected them to prompt further declines in corporate and household lending rates, thereby boosting economic confidence. translations.ecb38695fcc337db435f7c4d378d505045371eb6: On June 20, the People's Bank of China announced the latest loan prime rates (LPRs), lowering the one-year LPR to 3.55% and the LPR for terms of more than five years to 4.2%, both down 10 basis points from their previous values and ending the period of unchanged rates since September last year. translations.f191f533144f62f83f7ba95c212a9193bd32e119:
Xi Jinping, General Secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, President of China, Chairman of the Central Military Commission, and Director of the Central Commission for Comprehensively Deepening Reform, chaired the second meeting of the Central Commission for Comprehensively Deepening Reform on the afternoon of July 11. The meeting reviewed and approved the Opinions on Establishing a Higher-Standard Open-Economy System to Promote the Creation of a New Development Pattern, the Implementation Plan for Deepening Rural Reform, the Opinions on Promoting a Gradual Shift from Dual Controls on Energy Consumption to Dual Controls on Carbon Emissions, the Opinions on Piloting Reform of the Remuneration System at Higher-Education Institutions and Research Institutes, the Implementation Opinions on Further Deepening Reform of the Oil and Gas Market System and Enhancing the Country's Capacity to Safeguard Oil and Gas Security, and the Guiding Opinions on Deepening Power-System Reform and Accelerating the Establishment of a New Power System.

While chairing the meeting, Xi Jinping emphasised that establishing a higher-standard open-economy system was a strategic measure taken on China's own initiative to use opening up to promote reform and development. Centred on serving the creation of a new development pattern, emphasis must be placed on institutional opening up; reform of institutions and mechanisms must be deepened in key areas of external exchange and cooperation such as investment, trade, finance, and innovation; supporting policies and measures must be improved; and China's opening up must be raised proactively to a new level. The strategic goals of modernising agriculture and rural areas and building strength in agriculture must be firmly anchored. Properly handling the relationship between farmers and land must be the main thread, weak links in agricultural and rural development must be remedied more rapidly, and a solid foundation must be laid for fully building a modern socialist country. Based on the fact that China's development of an ecological civilisation had entered a critical period in which carbon reduction was the key strategic direction, regulation of the total amount and intensity of energy consumption must be improved and a gradual shift made towards a system of dual controls on the total amount and intensity of carbon emissions. Reform of the remuneration-distribution system for university teachers and research personnel must be treated as an important lever for advancing education, science and technology, and talent in a coordinated manner. A remuneration system that stimulates innovative vitality, is guided by the value of knowledge, has standardised and effective management, and balances safeguards and incentives must be gradually established to further stimulate the innovative and creative vitality of higher-education institutions and research institutes. Centred on the goal of enhancing the country's capacity to safeguard oil and gas security, reforms of institutions and mechanisms in the upstream, midstream, and downstream segments of the oil and gas industry must be advanced actively and prudently in response to prominent problems in the oil and gas system, ensuring a stable and reliable supply. Power-system reform must be deepened and construction of a new power system that is clean and low-carbon, safe and sufficient, economical and efficient, coordinated between supply and demand, flexible, and intelligent must be accelerated, to better promote the transformation of energy production and consumption and safeguard national energy security.

Li Qiang, Wang Huning, and Cai Qi, members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Deputy Directors of the Central Commission for Comprehensively Deepening Reform, attended the meeting.

The meeting stated that China's development currently faced a complex and severe international situation. The top-level design of the new open-economy system must be improved, reform of institutions and mechanisms in trade and investment deepened, market access expanded, the business environment comprehensively optimised, and service and safeguard systems improved. China's combined strengths must be brought fully into play, the domestic economic cycle used to attract global resources and factors of production, and the quality and level of trade and investment cooperation raised. Bottom-line and worst-case thinking must be upheld, the institutions and mechanisms safeguarding national security improved promptly, and capacity and standards for supervising opening up raised with a focus. Establishing a higher-standard open-economy system must be closely linked with national strategies such as high-quality joint construction of the Belt and Road, and China must actively participate in reform and development of the global governance system.

The meeting emphasised that, in implementing the arrangements made by the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China for deepening rural reform, efforts must focus on consolidating and improving the basic rural-management system, strengthening the food-security safeguard system, improving institutions and mechanisms for comprehensively advancing rural revitalisation, and improving the policy system for integrated urban-rural development. Breakthroughs and effective implementation of reforms in important areas and key links must be accelerated, giving farmers a greater sense of benefit from reform. Top-level design must be organically combined with grassroots exploration. Different regions must be permitted and encouraged to explore in light of local conditions, and there must be skill in identifying and summarising practical innovations at the grassroots level, with timely support provided when difficulties are encountered during exploration and innovation.

The meeting stated that, since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, green and low-carbon development, energy conservation, and emissions reduction had been given a prominent position. A system of dual controls on the total amount and intensity of energy consumption had been established and implemented, strongly promoting substantial improvement in China's energy-use efficiency and a continued decline in carbon-dioxide emissions intensity. In gradually shifting from dual controls on energy consumption to dual controls on carbon emissions, new systems must be established before old ones are abolished; the dual-control system for energy consumption must be improved; methods of regulation optimised and improved; foundational capacity for dual controls on carbon emissions strengthened; and the various supporting institutions for dual controls on carbon emissions improved, actively creating conditions for establishing and implementing a dual-control system for carbon emissions. The principle of prioritising conservation must be upheld consistently, energy conservation must be carried out to higher standards and with higher quality, and maximum benefits achieved at minimum cost. The pace of work must be kept steady, the relationship between development and emissions reduction coordinated, facts respected and actions kept within capabilities, and policy measures adjusted and optimised scientifically.

The meeting emphasised that, in conducting pilots of remuneration-system reform at higher-education institutions and research institutes, the distribution system must be optimised and standardised in line with remuneration-management needs and actual conditions, and the correct orientation for distribution established. A people-centred approach must be upheld, innovation given priority, and remuneration distribution closely linked to performance. Remuneration must be weighted towards personnel rooted on the front lines of teaching and research, undertaking difficult, urgent, dangerous, and important tasks, and making outstanding contributions; and towards those engaged in teaching basic disciplines and basic and frontier research, undertaking national tasks to achieve breakthroughs in key core technologies, and attaining major innovative achievements. Supervision of remuneration management must be strengthened to ensure that state funds are used where they are most needed for talent incentives and development of the relevant undertakings.

The meeting stated that reform of the oil and gas market system must be deepened further and systems for production, supply, storage, and sales strengthened. Market supervision must be intensified, sector-specific supervision and coordinated cross-sector supervision strengthened, order in the oil and gas market standardised, and fair competition promoted. Reform of the oil and gas reserve system must be deepened, and the emergency-response and regulatory capacities of reserves brought fully into play.

The meeting emphasised that the path for constructing the new power system must be designed scientifically and rationally, and that the share of traditional energy must be reduced gradually, in a planned and step-by-step manner, on the basis of safe and reliable substitution by new energy. Institutions and mechanisms suited to the new power system must be improved, and stronger innovation in power technology, market mechanisms, and business models promoted. Effective markets and a well-functioning government must be better combined, the policy system continuously improved, and the provision of basic public power services ensured.

Members of the Central Commission for Comprehensively Deepening Reform attended the meeting, and responsible officials from relevant central Party and state departments were present as non-voting participants.

translations.f779c8671774cb8de34c7aff2bd318d2d0f158a0: On June 29, the State Council issued the Measures for Advancing Institutional Opening Up by Aligning with High-Standard International Economic and Trade Rules in Eligible Pilot Free Trade Zones and Free Trade Ports, proposing 33 specific measures intended to promote trade in goods and services, facilitate the entry of business personnel, promote digital trade, optimise the business environment, and improve risk prevention and control, among other aims.
